items.title: Moderna enjoys stable vaccine sales thanks to global COVID uptake
items.snippet: While Moderna preps an entry to the oncology market next year with a personalized cancer vaccine, COVID sales are holding steady with several other vaccine launches underway around the world.

items.title: Voyager, C4 cut workforces
items.snippet: Follow along as BioSpace tracks job cuts and restructuring initiatives.

items.title: Forge’s Piteri-Molina on AI, Ohio and what’s next for gene therapy manufacturing
items.snippet: The BioSpace 40 Under 40 honoree helped steer Forge’s sale to Ajinomoto. Now, Samantha Piteri-Molina sees opportunities in AI-driven analytics and Ohio’s gene therapy ecosystem—with a responsibility to patients worldwide.

items.title: Agios axes 100-plus R&D roles while awaiting FDA decision
items.snippet: After the FDA delayed a decision for Agios Pharmaceuticals’ sickle cell disease candidate, the biopharma is letting go of more than 35% of its R&D employees.

items.title: Sarepta’s new CEO confident in clinical execution as DMD competitors close in
items.snippet: Sarepta Therapeutics’ newly minted CEO Michael Severino laid out his path to returning the muscular dystrophy therapy maker to the forefront of the rapidly expanding market.

items.title: Verdicts for Summit/Akeso, Capricor, Vertex mark FDA’s stacked November
items.snippet: Also lined up are target action dates for Sanofi’s Gaucher disease therapy, GSK’s lung cancer medicine and BridgeBio’s muscular dystrophy drug.

items.title: Merck, Moderna serve 99% of trial patients with mRNA vaccine as personalized shots near market
items.snippet: Personalized cancer vaccines are getting closer to market. Merck and Moderna just showed successful manufacturing in a large Phase 3 trial, proving they can deliver the goods.

items.title: Novartis confirms 9 reported cases of tumors in patients treated with Zolgensma
items.snippet: Advocates are sounding the alarm on social media as they learn from their doctors that Novartis has received reports of tumors in patients who have been treated with the spinal muscular atrophy gene therapy.

items.title: RevMed’s Rasonque shatters analyst estimates with $198M quarter
items.snippet: Pent-up demand for the new pancreatic cancer therapy Rasonque helped RevMed soar past analysts’ sales expectations and reach 5,000 patients in the third quarter.

items.title: T-time: British biotech pours $133M into the pot for bispecifics
items.snippet: With backing from three Big Pharma investment arms, British biotech T-Therapeutics is brewing up a clinical launch for its cancer and autoimmune T cell engagers.

items.title: Evommune inks molecular glue deal worth $1.1B biobucks to fill pipeline gap
items.snippet: Evommune is commiting $30 million upfront for Hinova Pharmaceuticals’ oral molecular glue degrader—a low-cost bet with a high probability of success, according to analysts, after clinical failures roiled the biotech’s internal pipeline earlier this year.

items.title: Coveted metabolic gem Rhythm reportedly gets $10B offer from AstraZeneca
items.snippet: AstraZeneca has apparently made a $10 billion bid to acquire Rhythm Pharmaceuticals, an offer William Blair suspects will not be the last for the hot ticket metabolic biotech.

items.title: Beyond the needle: The future of intratumoral therapy
items.snippet: In this episode of Denatured, you’ll hear from from Lewis Bender, CEO at Intensity Therapeutics and Paul-Peter Tak, president, CEO and board director at Candel Therapeutics. We explore how intratumoral therapies trigger systemic anticancer immunity from a local injection, and redefine a foundational platform in immuno...

items.title: The top 12 companies hiring in biopharma now
items.snippet: Average jobs live on BioSpace increased year over year in October, a good sign for those eyeing a new position. If that’s you, check out the list of which companies are most actively looking to hire.

items.title: A treatment revolution is underway in MASH
items.snippet: To build on the momentum in MASH, we—at Madrigal Pharmaceuticals and the industry more widely—must further expand approaches to diagnosis, monitoring and individualized treatment to help more patients.

items.title: 1 in 5 have had multiple biopharma layoffs, poll finds
items.snippet: Biotech and pharma professionals share job hunt challenges after being let go, while a recruiting expert discusses why hiring managers prefer candidates without employment gaps and how to address gaps in interviews.

items.title: Boehringer bets big on China, offering $7B biobucks for Sino cancer programs
items.snippet: Boehringer Ingelheim is building up its China strategy, inking a deal to develop new cancer treatments with Sino Biopharmaceutical just weeks after opening an R&D facility in Shanghai.

items.title: AbbVie bets up to $1.47B for Nxera’s discarded IBD program
items.snippet: AbbVie’s $100 million upfront cash payment will purchase global rights to Nxera’s deprioritized oral small molecule, which has already completed Phase 1 testing.

items.title: Amgen starts MariTide autoinjector study as pivotal readouts approach
items.snippet: With the first Phase 3 data expected for Amgen’s MariTide next year, analysts are looking for evidence that the GLP-1 candidate is tolerable. Meanwhile, the company has begun testing an autoinjector formulation.

items.title: Sanofi’s axing of Nurix STAT6 program ‘not a target-related issue’
items.snippet: Sanofi has discontinued an early-stage STAT6 degrader program licensed from Nurix Therapeutics, a decision analysts say is related to the asset itself or Sanofi’s strategic reprioritization rather than the drug class more broadly.

items.title: Eli Lilly and the LA Dodgers: A tale of 2 dynasties
items.snippet: Watching the baseball playoffs this week, I was struck by the parallels between the Los Angeles Dodgers and Eli Lilly. Both franchises spend a lot of money and always appear to come out on top.

items.title: After Novartis’ devastating M&A losses, long live the executive willing to try
items.snippet: Big Pharma needs more—not fewer—bold bets on rare and difficult diseases after Novartis’ efforts to invest in muscular dystrophy and ALS hit major roadblocks this month.

items.title: Mikhail, Davis embody the FDA’s stabilization, Seehafer signals AI revolution is coming
items.snippet: Newly solidified in their roles as the heads of CBER and CDER, Karim Mikhail and Michael Davis have been working for months to right the ship that had begun to capsize under former Commissioner Marty Makary. Meanwhile, Jared Seehafer will become the first-ever deputy commissioner focused on artificial intelligence.

items.title: Chaotic adcomms threaten to derail FDA’s bid to renew trust after Makary, Prasad
items.snippet: The FDA has been trying to mend fences with rare disease drug developers and patient groups since the departure of former Commissioner Marty Makary three months ago. But advisory committee meetings last week for Replimune and Capricor Therapeutics only created more confusion and frustration.
